take_homes: Naming a framework and saying 'tune it for Z' gets a better result than pasting its questions. The hate-list inversion, with specific gripes, also sharpened the output a lot.
The agent grades its own work too kindly. A fresh reader with only the output as context gives a harder read, and I should use that in how our engineers review agent output.
The model didn't improve over the session. Better context made the output better, and a rules file is how that survives into the next session.

monday.move: Add a cold-reader step to our agent review flow: a second agent that sees only the output, not the work that produced it. I'll also try the rules-file move with one non-engineer, probably someone in sales, on their own material.
monday.who: Me and two senior engineers for the review step. One sales lead for the rules file.
monday.when: Review step Monday morning. Sales lead later in the week, if I find the time.
monday.stop_condition: The cold reader flags nothing real across ten outputs, so it's ceremony. Or the sales lead doesn't ask for a second session.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for this. I haven't worked out who would maintain a rules file for sales. I may also skip the check step myself because the output looks fine.

misconception.why: The agent's own look-back was soft, and my own read looked fine too. That makes the claim that checking is for beginners harder to hold. I still skipped the review in most phases, so I leave only partly shaken.

one_line: The first half is for people who haven't used an agent. The hate-list trick and the point that the model flatters its own work were worth the day.
